title: Conserved and divergent features of blastoderm patterning and anterior segmentation across insects
authors: Rosen, M., Sheizaf, I., & Chipman, A. D.
abstract: We investigate how the anterior blastoderm is established in hemimetabolous insects compared to holometabolous models, identifying a core conserved network of gap-like transcription factors directing cephalic furrow formation.

title: Evolution of the arthropod head: morphological transitions and gene regulatory homology
abstract: A synthesis of recent comparative embryological and genomic findings addressing the segmental composition of the anterior arthropod body and the origins of cephalic novelties.

title: Posterior growth zone oscillations and Wnt/Notch dynamics during sequential segment formation
authors: Green, E., Levin, D., Akam, M., & Chipman, A. D.
abstract: Demonstrating that rhythmic pulses of Wnt signaling coordinate cell division and segment boundary allocation in the posterior growth zone of short-germ insects.

title: Phylogeography and endemism of the Levantine terrestrial invertebrate fauna across climatic transitions
abstract: Analysis of museum collections revealing deep genetic divergences and micro-refugia in Mediterranean-desert ecotones of the Levant.

title: Comparative microRNA genomics across Panarthropoda illuminates deep regulatory innovations
authors: Shaked, Y., Cohen, A., & Chipman, A. D.
abstract: Comprehensive cataloging of conserved and novel microRNA families across centipedes, crustaceans, and insects.

title: The first myriapod genome sequence reveals conservative arthropod gene architecture and unique adaptations
authors: Chipman, A. D., Ferrier, D. E. K., Brena, C., Qu, J., et al.
abstract: The genome sequence of the centipede Strigamia maritima provides a crucial baseline for the ancestral arthropod genome, displaying remarkable conservation of gene synteny and ancestral developmental pathways.

title: Parallel evolution of segmentation mechanisms in arthropods and vertebrates
abstract: Examining whether rhythmic segmentation mechanisms in bilateria are derived from a common ancestral clock or represent recurrent evolutionary convergence.

title: The evolution of the segmentation process in arthropods: insights from centipedes and onychophorans
authors: Chipman, A. D., Arthur, W., & Akam, M.
abstract: Demonstrating how posterior addition of segments in geophilomorph centipedes sheds light on the primitive mode of arthropod developmental patterning.
